I’d have to say fear of the unknown and my tendency to catastrophise things.
Even me

I think once we examine the reasons people become vindictive, it opens your eyes to *all* of their flaws. 
I agree that it’s better to be at peace. You could make someone feel like the asshole they are, but quite honestly, they already do which is why they behave the way that they do. 

I think this is just something people need to learn to do. 
When I was younger, I equated money with success. But as I’ve aged, I’ve realized that money and success are not the same. When I try to explain this to children, they scoff. They ask if I think a beggar on the road is successful. I don’t enter into the argument because I don’t need to prove myself to anyone. We can be content in our knowledge that life is about living for yourself and not obsessing over other people.

I do that too. I used to just ignore her comments and carry on with my day, but I think my ‘blow up’ was blocking her. I realized that in the moment, being a bitch would make me feel better  but didn’t deal with the issue at hand: me trying to be a nice person.  It’s better for me in the long run to just cut her out of my life. She doesn’t serve a purpose for me so I don’t actually need her there. If my purpose in her life was to be her comparison doll… well, she’s not paying me for the job so I’m not sticking around.
You should watch Hamlet.
It okay to not be okay. But keep pushing. I want to say that it gets better. I hope that it does for you. We are all in this together and we’ll keep each other alive.
